title: Iterated coupling inequality
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $\lambda$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, let $\kappa$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega\times\Omega$, and let $p,q\in\mathbb R$. Suppose that for every pair of functions $f,g:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, the expectation of $f(x)g(y)$ when $(x,y)$ has law $\kappa$ is at most the product of the $p$- and $q$-norms of $f$ and $g$ under $\lambda$. Then for every natural number $n$ and all functions $F,G:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, the iterated coupling inner product of $F$ and $G$ is at most the product of their iterated $p$- and $q$-norms, respectively.

the stated single-coordinate coupling inequality holds for every $f,g:\Omega\to\mathbb R$
